text:
michelle: hitting a weird ordering bug in the browser sampleapp when I reconnect really fast. final [DONE] arrives, client closes stream, then a later chunk arrives and we blow up on JSON parse. repro: Chrome, latest js sampleapp, proxy in front of API; abort + reconnect within ~100ms. anyone seen this?

ben: ugh. which SDK and proxy?

michelle: js sampleapp (main), proxy is our local dev proxy (http/1). logs show a chunk that comes after the stream terminated. pasting snippet below.

michelle: ```
data: {"id":"tok1","delta":"hello"}
data: {"id":"tok2","delta":" world"}
data: [DONE]
data: {"id":"tok2","delta":"!"}
```

sara: that sequence is wild. could the proxy be buffering and flushing out-of-order on reconnect? we did change socket options recently.

ben: we rely on SSE semantics + last-event-id for resume. if an intermediary buffers then replays, the client may observe a late fragment after the delimiter. we tried to avoid adding per-chunk metadata to keep SDK parity.

ryan: i can repro locally by toggling Nagle/flush on the proxy. if a small packet flushes after the server already signalled done, the client sees the final delimiter then the late packet.

michelle: workaround for now: adding a 250ms delay before reconnect avoids it. not great for UX though.

sara: options: 1) server emits explicit seq numbers in each data frame (breaks parity), 2) client ignores any data after [DONE] until new stream, 3) fix proxy to preserve strict ordering and flush semantics.

ben: client-side small fix seems least invasive: on JS SDK treat any bytes after [DONE] in same eventstream as suspect and drop unless they create a new stream. can we centralize that logic so other SDKs mirror it?

ryan: i'll open an issue and add a small test in sampleapp that does fast reconnects. tagging eng-runtime for kernel/flush behavior.

deploy-bot: Issue created: #4567 - "browser sampleapp: late chunk after [DONE] on fast reconnect" (reported by ryan)

michelle: :thumbsup: thanks. filing a follow-up to track a longer-term fix (server/proxy change) and a short-term client guard.

ben: ok assigning to eng-runtime for triage. also let's add a note to the onboarding sampleapp README about the reconnect timing quirk so folks don't get stuck.

sara: agree. adding "quick-reconnect can surface buffered chunks" note to the README is low friction.

ryan: will push a tiny PR for the README + test and link the issue.

michelle: great, thanks everyone.
